items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: I used to go there around 11 o'clock... they'd get up about that time... Pee-wee was, well, he was here for quite a while with Lurie Primer

ctx.x: Yeah, Jimmy McPartland was the trumpet player. It was sounding good.

Yeah, Pee-wee, Pee-wee's nose, really, really russling the mind. Is he? Yeah, Pee-wee, when I first went to New York, he was doing a lot of recording with Nichols and those guys. Yeah, yeah. And then the other time, he and Bix were living together.

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: I used to go there around 11 o'clock... they'd get up about that time... I lived on 53rd and Broadway.

ctx.x: Yeah, Pee-wee, Russell and Bix were living together. Must have been quite a household. At the 44th Street Hotel in New York, and they had a little yacht, you used to call them yacht pianos in those days. Really, two and a half octave piano. So they'd get, I used to go there around 11 o'clock. I lived on 53rd and Broadway. And I used to go there around 11, 12 o'clock, and they'd get up about that time, you know. And they'd have to sit the gin sitting on the bed table, you know, and they'd get up, and they'd go in…
